title: operator_identity — each candidate resolved from a device symbol to a source location
description:
`items/text.json` of the `operator_identity` handoff. Written against the real sealed artefact at `cheat_for_mock/stage3-analyze/operator_identity/` (two operators, both `symbol_search`, both with an empty `target_kernel_functions`).

**The field names are AgentKernelArena's `config.yaml` vocabulary and are not invented here** — `image_repo_path`, `repo_subdir`, `repository_language`, `source_file_path`, `editable_sources`, `target_kernel_functions`, `kernel_identity`. Adopting an existing vocabulary is what lets the next step emit Arena-shaped output with no translation layer, and renaming any of them here would create one.

**What this document is for, stated because it is easy to get backwards.** `check_identity_resolved` runs with `min_resolve_ratio: 0.0`, on purpose: the evidence available is a device symbol, and for a Tensile GEMM dispatched from C++ there is no Python frame to find. A floor above zero fails a correct analysis on exactly the kernels the next stage excludes anyway. So what is checked — and what this schema makes checkable — is that **uncertainty is modelled rather than absent**:

1. An operator that resolved to no source file must carry a `resolution_hint` saying where to look. Silence is the one answer not permitted.
2. `source_resolution_method: agent_recovered` means the resolver gave a direction and no entry point; it therefore requires a hint too. It is not a failure — it is the path two of Arena's own samples took.
3. `image_repo_path` is a `${PLACEHOLDER}` and never a path. `handoff/locality.py` refuses the seal over a container-absolute root like `/sgl-workspace`, and this pattern is that rule made mechanical one step earlier, where it names the field instead of failing the whole delivery.

**What a schema cannot do and `check_identity_resolved` therefore does**: compute `summary.resolve_ratio` from `operators` and check the stored figure follows from it. A document that disagrees with itself is the one failure a required-property list cannot express.

schema_version.description: As in `kernel_worklist.schema.json`: the one field the sealed artefact lacks, added rather than dropped.

resolver.description: What instrument was available, recorded whether or not it worked. On the sealed run `kernel_finder` was `unavailable` with `reason: magpie root absent` and both operators resolved anyway, by symbol search — which is the case that makes the distinction worth keeping: an empty result from an absent tool and an empty result from a tool that ran are not the same finding.

reason.description: Required in spirit when `kernel_finder` is `unavailable`; enforced below.

container_root_placeholders.description: Every placeholder used anywhere in `operators`, with a one-line description of what it holds. The **descriptions, not the expansions** — an expansion is a container-absolute path and would refuse the seal. What each expands to for a given image lives in the producing package's `assets/lib/container_roots.yaml`; the framework has a mechanism for this (`Oracles.image_prefixes` against a kind's `dependencies`) and it is not wired up, which is recorded as a bug rather than worked around here.

resolve_ratio.description: `resolved / operators`. Reported and **not** gated at production time: `check_identity_resolved`'s floor is 0.0 and the reasons are in this file's header.

operators.description: One entry per **selected** kernel from `kernel_worklist` — the rejected rows are not resolved, because resolving a collective nobody will optimise is work with no consumer.

name.description: The device symbol, verbatim, as in the worklist.

logical_operator.description: The name a human uses for the operation, and the `workset.operators[].operator_id` downstream. **The unit of work is this, not `name`**: a device symbol is frequently a generated string that appears nowhere in the checkout — the sealed artefact's own case is `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp4_wfp4_bf16_g1u1`, whose `_g1u1` suffix belongs to a different naming scheme entirely and whose generator never emits it.

image_repo_path.description: A placeholder, never a path. See the header, rule 3. Every value here must be a key of `container_root_placeholders`, which is a cross-field rule and `check_identity_resolved`'s to enforce.

repository_language.description: `ck`, `triton`, `python`, `cuda`, `hip`, `tilelang`, … what the editable source is written in, which is what selects the KernelForge fellow.

source_file_path.description: Repo-relative, and may be empty — see the biconditional below. Never absolute.

editable_sources.description: The subset an optimiser is permitted to change. Usually equal to `source_file_path` and deliberately a separate field: a kernel can be readable in five files and safely editable in one.

target_kernel_functions.description: The entry points. **Legitimately empty here** — the sealed artefact has it empty for both operators — because this step resolves by symbol and the next one reads the source to fill it in. It must be non-empty by the time it reaches `workset.operators[].edit_target.entry_function`, and that is where it is enforced. Splitting it this way keeps 'the symbol did not resolve' (normal) apart from 'the entry function was never found' (a problem).

source_resolution_method.description: How the location was established, strongest first. `trace_python_stack` is the profiler's own frames; `symbol_search` matched the symbol against source text; `agent_recovered` means a reader gave a direction and no entry point; `declared` means it was known a priori. The third is **not a failure** — it is the path Arena's TileLang and KDA samples both took.

resolution_hint.description: Where to look next. Required whenever nothing resolved; see the biconditional below.

resolution_probe.description: The string actually searched for, when the method was `symbol_search`. Kept because a probe that is a *shortening* of the symbol — as here — is a weaker match than an exact one, and a reader cannot tell without it.

resolution_evidence.description: Why the match is believed. Prose, and prose is right: this is an argument.

excluded_reason.description: Set when this operator was selected by the ranker and then found unworkable here. An alternative to `resolution_hint` for satisfying the biconditional: 'look here next' and 'do not look' are both answers, and only silence is not.

launcher.description: The Python frame that dispatched it, when one was traced. `{}` when none was, which is the common case and is not a defect.

baseline_ref_symbol.description: The correctness reference, if one was located here. Frequently empty at this step and filled by the next, which is why `workset.operators[].reference` is required there and not here. When it can be filled, `kind: imported` is strongly preferred: a reference written from a reading of the kernel is how a correctness gate comes to agree with a bug.

test_file.description: The framework's own test for this kernel, when one exists. Worth more than it looks: on the sealed run it is how the reference for one operator was found at all, because the project's end-to-end test checks the same kernel against the same function.

cases.description: Carried through from the worklist unchanged. This step resolves locations; it does not re-derive shapes, and a shape list that changed between the two artefacts would mean one of them was edited independently.

allOf.$comment:
The one rule this document exists to enforce, and the reason min_resolve_ratio can be 0.0 without the validator becoming decorative. An operator that resolved to no source file must say where to look next, or say why not to. Unresolved-and-silent is the only state refused.

Written as `if (unresolved AND no excluded_reason) then resolution_hint` rather than the more obvious `anyOf` of the two, because an `anyOf` failure reports 'is not valid under any of the given schemas' and dumps the whole operator — naming neither field. The producer reading that message cannot tell what to add. This form names `resolution_hint`.
`agent_recovered` is by definition 'a direction and no entry point'. A direction that is not written down is not a direction.
A symbol search that found nothing to search for is not a symbol search.
